Alice: Heads up — onboarding OrpheusX-2B int4: we see a deterministic quality drop at long context (>4096). FP16 baseline perplexity 12.3, int4 after conversion 15.9, but loss spikes when sequence >4096 tokens. Anyone seen rotary frequency aliasing or tokenizer oddness like this? :thinking:
Ben: Hmm. Frequency aliasing is a common culprit for longctx divergence. Do we have the model config vs conversion logs?
Alice: Pasted minimal repro and conversion command below. small repro: generate 9k tokens from a long wiki dump and measure ppl. Conversion: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py --src orpheusx2b/ --dst converted/orpheusx2b-int4/ --quant int4 --backend hf_q8
```
Log shows default rotary_scale used by converter = 1.0 while model config lists rotary_scale ~1.68.
Chloe: That mismatch would absolutely drift phase over long sequences. The converter should preserve rotary base/freq. Can you dump model_config.json?
Alice: model_config.json snippet: 
```
{"architectures": ["OrpheusXForCausalLM"],
 "rotary_emb": {"base": 10000, "scale": 1.6843},
 "vocab_size": 50288}
```
converter log snippet: 
```
[INFO] rotary_scale: not found, using default 1.0
[WARN] head_dim inferred from weights: 64
```
Ben: Yikes. Converter bug. It shouldn't default when key exists. Might be subtle key name: converter looks for "rotary_freq" whereas newer model uses "rotary_emb.scale".
Emily: Also saw strange tokenizer behavior for sequences containing emoji + ZWJ ligatures. Tokenizer splitting the flag/transgender sequence into extra sentinel-like tokens which inflates KV cache positions. Example: 
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("🏳️‍⚧️ long story...")
[2341, 9123, 0, 0, 4099, 123]
```
The 0s look like sentinel/pad-like IDs. Onboard tests show these are actually separate tokens representing ZWJ components.
Dave: That'll shift token ids between tokenizer and model embed table if normalization differs during conversion. Are we normalizing to NFKC anywhere?
Alice: Converter uses NFC by default, our tokenizer was trained on NFKC-normalized inputs. So normalization mismatch + rotary_scale mismatch = compounded drift.
Chloe: Two fixes: 1) ensure converter preserves rotary_emb.scale and maps it to runtime kernel param, 2) normalize input consistently (force NFKC) or fold ZWJ sequences into single token using tokenizer postprocess.
Ben: Quick check — run a headwise-phase-delta test to see where aliasing starts. I have a small script: 
```
python tools/rotary_check.py --model converted/orpheusx2b-int4/ --input tests/long_wiki.txt --maxlen 8192
```
Output snippet: 
```
[INFO] head 0..1: ok
[WARN] head 3: phase_offset drift @ pos 4096 -> 0.12 rad
[WARN] head 7: alias wrap detected @ pos 6144
```
Alice: Ran it after forcing rotary_scale=1.6843 in converted config. Phase drift gone in those heads, but perplexity still 14.0 (better than 15.9).
Infra Bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/1712349999/convert-logs.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Chloe: For the tokenizer ZWJ issue, try sanitizer step: `text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text)` before tokenization. Also consider adding a small post-tokenizer merge rule for known emoji sequences.
Emily: I tried NFKC normalization + re-run batch eval on 1k examples: int4 ppl -> 13.6 (with rotary fix still applied). That closes most gap.
Ben: Nice. Still a delta vs fp16 12.3 but within expected quantization hit. Did we check attention kernel scaling in int4 runtime? Sometimes per-head scale is applied differently.
Dave: Kernel applies per-tensor scale for int4 sym/asym options. Our conversion used symmetric by default; try asymmetric (preserves mean). Quick command: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py --src orpheusx2b/ --dst converted/orpheusx2b-int4-asym/ --quant int4 --quant-mode asymmetric --preserve-rotary-scale
```
Then rerun the rotary_check and batch eval.
Alice: Ran asymmetric + preserve-rotary-scale + NFKC. Final numbers: ppl int4 -> 13.1, longctx stability good to 8k, headwise phase deltas <0.01 rad. Latency unchanged.
Chloe: Great. Action items: 1) Patch converter to look for rotary_emb.scale and rotary_emb.base aliases, and add `--preserve-rotary-scale` flag (PR queued), 2) Default tokenizer pipeline should include NFKC normalization for models that trained with it, 3) Add a quick rotary-interop check to onboarding CI (script above).
Ben: I'll file the conversion PR and add unit test. Emily, can you own tokenizer sanity fix?
Emily: Yep, will open a PR with tests for ZWJ emoji sequences + normalization.
Dave: I'll add the rotary_check.py to nightly onboards and hook infra-bot to post warnings when headwise phase >0.05 rad.
Alice: Thanks team. Saved a bunch of time. Leaving notes in the model onboarding doc and creating ticket RED-1234 for follow-ups. :rocket:
Ben: :thumbsup:
Infra Bot: deploy status: nightly-onboard triggered for orpheusx2b-int4-asym — job 987654 started.
Emily: Quick FYI — odd corner: some downstream evals (summarization ROUGE) still show small regressions (~1.5 pts). We should monitor before promoting to dedicated.
Alice: Agreed. We'll run the full eval suite and regressions before approving.
